\begin{document}

\title{Computational Identification and Audit of Third-MUB Loci Within Karlsson's Three-Parameter Family}

\author{%
\IEEEauthorblockN{Adian Jaupi}%
}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
I document a reproducible per-$H$ computational pipeline for mutually unbiased basis (MUB) extendability inside Karlsson's three-parameter family $K_6^{(3)}$ only, together with a computational identification of third-MUB loci in audited search sets.
Within a certified search CSV ($928$ rows, $899$ pool-complete) and HP re-verification, the only reproducing third-MUB loci found are the $F_6$ $\theta{=}0$ bounded $\lambda$-arc and the Dita full $\lambda$-circle (Finding~\ref{thm:trackd})---an identification of the audited search, not a theorem on all of $K_6^{(3)}$.
Supporting HP probes (Findings~\ref{prop:L5},~\ref{prop:L6},~\ref{thm:T2}), the $\mathcal{S}^*$ primary sweep ($1863/1865$ candidates, no fourth MUB observed), a documented $512$-point coarse-grid miss of every known third-MUB locus, pool-completeness tables, and reproduction pins are included so the report is independently citable as methodology.
Certified fourth-MUB obstruction at seven Dita points and exact $D_0$ re-verification appear in the companion theorems paper~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026}; confirmatory negatives here do not replace that certificate.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
Complex Hadamard matrices, Karlsson family, mutually unbiased bases, homotopy continuation, reproducible computation, computational audit
\end{IEEEkeywords}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

Mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) in $\mathbb{C}^d$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
    \label{eq:mu}
    \bigl|\langle\psi|\phi\rangle\bigr|^2 = \frac{1}{d}
\end{equation}
for vectors from distinct bases~\cite{Bengtsson2007, Brierley2009}.
In dimension six, Zauner conjectured $N(6)=3$~\cite{Zauner1999, Scott2010}.
Complex Hadamard matrices (CHMs) supply second bases; Karlsson's family $K_6(\theta,\phi,\lambda)$~\cite{Karlsson2011} is a three-parameter source of $6\times6$ CHMs treated in the composite-dimension MUB review of McNulty--Weigert~\cite{McNulty2026}.
Grassl~\cite{Grassl2004} showed that searches must be \emph{per} Hadamard matrix, not via a fixed pool unbiased only to $F_6$.

This companion report is a stand-alone computational methodology and audit document.
Its primary contributions are: (i)~a corrected per-$H$ homotopy/clique pipeline with formal search sets; (ii)~computational identification of two reproducing third-MUB loci in audited data; (iii)~honest negative evidence on larger sets, including a self-correcting $512$-point grid miss that warns against over-reading sweep negatives.
Algebraic gauge structure and the certified/exact fourth-MUB theorems are proved in the companion theorems paper~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026}.

\subsection{Contributions}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[\textbf{M1}] Reproducible per-$H$ MU-pool pipeline, completeness gate, planted-clique validation, and formal sets $\mathcal{S}_{588}$, $\mathcal{S}^*$, $\mathcal{R}$.
    \item[\textbf{M2}] Computational identification of third-MUB loci in the certified search (Finding~\ref{thm:trackd}; F6 $\theta{=}0$ arc and Dita $\lambda$-circle), with HP support (Findings~\ref{prop:L5},~\ref{prop:L6},~\ref{thm:T2}).
    \item[\textbf{M3}] Audit trail: $512$-point coarse-grid miss; $\mathcal{S}^*$ sweep; pool-completeness tables; reproduction appendix.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Background}
\label{sec:background}

Let $H$ be a $6\times6$ CHM. Normalized columns form a basis mutually unbiased to the computational basis.
Karlsson's family is written as in~\cite{Karlsson2011, McNulty2026}; the companion theorems paper records the gauge algebra used below~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026}.
I use Karlsson's original $A$-matrix formulas throughout (the McNulty--Weigert transcription fails numerical CHM tests; see~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026}).

\section{Methods}
\label{sec:methods}

\subsection{Problem Formulation}
For fixed $H$, seek unit vectors $v\in\mathbb{C}^6$ unbiased to $\mathcal{B}_I$ and $\mathcal{B}_H$.
With gauge $v_0=1$ and variables $z_i=v_i\sqrt{6}$ ($i=1,\ldots,5$), computational unbiasedness yields $|z_i|=1$, encoded as $z_i w_i=1$ with auxiliary variables $w_i\approx\bar z_i$ on the conjugate locus.

Unbiasedness to column $k$ of $H$ requires
\begin{equation}
    \label{eq:colmu}
    \Bigl|\sum_{j=0}^{5}\overline{H_{j,k}}\,z_j\Bigr|^2=6
    \;\Longleftrightarrow\;
    \Bigl(\sum_{j}\overline{H_{j,k}}z_j\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_{j}H_{j,k}w_j\Bigr)=6.
\end{equation}
I impose~\eqref{eq:colmu} for $k=0,\ldots,4$; column $k=5$ is dependent by Parseval once $H/\sqrt{6}$ is unitary and $w_i=\bar z_i$.
The system has $10$ equations in $10$ unknowns and \emph{depends on $H$}.

\textbf{Critical convention:}~\eqref{eq:colmu} uses \emph{column} index $k$ ($H_{j,k}$), not row index.

\subsection{Root Finding}
I use HomotopyContinuation.jl~\cite{HomotopyContinuation} with fresh polyhedral solves (mixed volume $252$) and parameter homotopy from $F_6$, with fresh-solve fallback when tracking drops solutions.

\subsection{Four-MUB Extension Test}
Given pool $\mathcal{P}$:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Orthogonality graph on $\mathcal{P}$ (edge if $|\langle v,w\rangle|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ortho}}$).
    \item \texttt{found\_third} $\Leftrightarrow$ a clique of size $\ge6$ exists.
    \item For each $6$-clique $B_3$, filter for a second $6$-clique $\Rightarrow$ \texttt{found\_fourth}.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Validation Protocol}
Before sweeping, I require:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[\textbf{V1}] At $H=F_6$: $156$ raw roots, $48$ deduplicated pool vectors~\cite{Haagerup2001, Bjork2015}.
    \item[\textbf{V2}] Homotopy-with-fallback restores full pool when tracking drops roots.
    \item[\textbf{V3}] At generic $K_6(0.3,0.5,0.2)$: pool size $48$, $\texttt{max\_clique}=2$.
    \item[\textbf{V4}] At Dita $(\arccos(1/\sqrt{3}),\pi/4,0.4)$: pool $\in\{48,72,120\}$~\cite{Brierley2009}.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation}
\label{sec:impl}

The pipeline is implemented in Julia~1.12.6 (HomotopyContinuation~2.22, Graphs~1.14) with Python helpers:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{src/mub\_zauner\_6d\_liang\_chen.jl} --- core solver, extension test, pool completeness;
    \item \texttt{validate\_perH\_pipeline.jl}, \texttt{audit\_clique\_pipeline.jl} --- validation and planted-clique audits;
    \item \texttt{sweep\_karlsson.jl}, \texttt{search\_special\_loci.jl} --- coarse and certified parameter sweeps;
    \item \texttt{locus\_classification.jl}, \texttt{validate\_third\_mub\_candidates.jl} --- Track~D HP identification;
    \item \texttt{dita\_lambda\_fourth\_dense.jl}, \texttt{fourth\_mub\_locus\_sweep.jl} --- Track~A/C fourth-MUB probes;
    \item \texttt{karlsson\_k6\_3.py}, \texttt{chm\_equivalence.py}, \texttt{finish\_project\_audit.py}.
\end{itemize}
Reproduction commands and search-set definitions are in \texttt{REPRODUCE.md} and \texttt{docs/SEARCH\_SETS.md}.

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Validation}
All checks V1--V4 passed (\texttt{validate\_perH\_pipeline.jl}).
At $F_6$ the fresh solve returned $156$ raw solutions and $48$ pool vectors after conjugate-locus filtering and deduplication.

\subsection{Coarse Parameter Sweep (Superseded)}
\label{sec:coarsesweep}
I initially swept $\theta,\phi\in[0.02,\pi-0.02]$ and $\lambda\in[0,2\pi)$ on an $8\times8\times8$ grid ($512$ points).
Table~\ref{tab:sweep} summarizes that run; \textbf{it must not be read as exhaustive}.
The grid avoided $\theta=0$ and missed the Dita point $(\theta,\phi,\lambda)\approx(0.955,\pi/4,0.4)$.
\texttt{found\_fourth}=\texttt{false} on this grid is therefore not evidence of absence: the same run also reported \texttt{found\_third}=\texttt{false} at every point, which was false.

At $F_6$, HomotopyContinuation \texttt{certify} yields \textbf{156 distinct certified} roots (mixed volume $252$); \texttt{pool\_completeness\_report} gives \texttt{pool\_complete\_flag=true} with $48$ deduplicated pool vectors.
A full re-certification of all $512$ coarse-grid points found \textbf{$512/512$} satisfy the corrected completeness gate ($n_{\mathrm{certified}}=n_{\mathrm{tracked}}$); none had \texttt{max\_clique}$\ge3$.
Certification validates the MU-pool polynomial system, not clique number or fourth-MUB existence.

The sole M\"obius degeneracy candidate from \texttt{degeneracy\_scan.py} coincides with the Dita anchor; rounded $10$-digit coordinates yield \texttt{max\_clique}$=2$ while exact Dita parameters yield \texttt{max\_clique}$=6$.
Witness-set and NID probes at $F_6$ and Dita confirm the \emph{per-$H$} MU-pool system is zero-dimensional ($156$ and $\sim240$ certified isolated roots; Finding~\ref{lem:L7}).
A $20\times20$ grid at fixed Dita~$\theta$ found $0/400$ clique-$6$ hits because grid points omit exact $\phi=\pi/4$; targeted $\phi$-offset sweeps (Table~\ref{tab:phisweep}) give clique-$6$ only at $\phi=\pi/4$ and drop to clique-$2$ for $|\Delta\phi|\ge10^{-3}$ at all nine values.
At $F_6(\theta{=}0,\lambda{=}0.3)$, clique-$6$ along $\lambda$ drops at $|\Delta\lambda|{=}0.0550448$ ($+$) and $0.0625984$ ($-$) (arc width $\approx0.118$).
Detailed probe statistics appear in Appendix~\ref{app:probes} (Tables~\ref{tab:locusdim}--\ref{tab:phisweep}).

\subsection{Certified Search Set \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{S}_{588}$}{S588} and Extended CSV}
I define the \textbf{certified search set} $\mathcal{S}\subset K_6^{(3)}$ as points with \texttt{pool\_complete\_flag}=\texttt{true} and $n_{\text{certified}} = n_{\text{tracked}}$.
The design target $\mathcal{S}_{588}$ is documented in \repo{../overview/REPRODUCE.md}.
The on-disk CSV \repo{results/special_loci_search.csv} contains $928$ certified rows ($899$ pool-complete, $0$ with \texttt{found\_fourth}=\texttt{true}) as of 2026-08-05.
Reproducible third-MUB anchors: $F_6$ at $\theta=0$ and Dita; $\theta=\pi/2$ \texttt{circulant\_match} rows are \textbf{tolerance artifacts} ($\texttt{max\_clique}=6$ at $\texttt{ortho\_tol}=10^{-8}$ but $2$ at $10^{-12}$).
\textbf{$\mathcal{S}^*$ phased batches:} authoritative full primary sweep $1863/1865$ distinct points, \texttt{found\_fourth}=\texttt{false} throughout (\repo{special_loci_degen1845.meta.txt}).

\subsection{Main Computational Finding: Computational Identification of Third-MUB Loci}
\label{sec:trackd}
\textbf{Track~D (contribution M2)---computational identification of the audited search, not a theorem.}
I catalogued HP-verified clique-$6$ rows via \repo{locus_classification.jl}.
Of $45$ sweep candidates with $\texttt{max\_clique}\ge6$, \textbf{36} survive 256-bit clique re-verification; \textbf{9} $\theta=\pi/2$ \texttt{circulant\_match} rows fail HP.
Clustering by locus proximity yields \textbf{two reproducing components} only:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{F6\_theta0 arc:} $\theta=0$, bounded $\lambda$-interval (width $\approx0.118$); $\phi$ is a gauge coordinate~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026} ($27$ HP rows).
    \item \textbf{Dita $\lambda$-circle:} $\theta=\arccos(1/\sqrt{3})$, $\phi=\pi/4$, clique-$6$ on the full $\lambda$ circle; $\lambda$ is a matrix-level moduli direction with $\pi$-periodic CHM class~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026} ($9$ HP rows).
\end{itemize}
CHM-equivalence between cluster representatives gives minimum residual $\approx5.24$ (F6\_theta0 vs.\ Dita), confirming \textbf{distinct} components.
Full JSON output: \repo{results/locus_classification.json}.
No additional HP-verified third-MUB components appeared in the certified search CSV ($928$ rows) or the $\mathcal{S}^*$ primary sweep ($1863$ candidate points).
This is an identification of the \emph{audited} search, not a proof that no other loci exist in $K_6^{(3)}$.

\begin{finding}[Third-MUB loci in certified search]
\label{thm:trackd}
Within the certified search CSV ($928$ rows), HP re-verification of clique-$6$ candidates, and Track~D clustering, the only reproducing third-MUB loci found are, up to parametrization gauge:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item the $F_6$ $\theta{=}0$ bounded $\lambda$-arc (width $\approx0.118$ rad), and
    \item the Dita full $\lambda$-circle at $\phi=\pi/4$ ($\lambda$ moduli direction; $\pi$-periodic CHM class).
\end{enumerate}
Nine $\theta=\pi/2$ \texttt{circulant\_match} CSV rows are non-reproducing under HP.
\end{finding}

\subsection{Fourth-MUB Negative Evidence (Confirmatory; Track~C, Track~A)}
\label{sec:trackc}
Beyond the pointwise certified obstruction of the companion theorems paper~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026}, this subsection records confirmatory negative numerics on larger audited sets; Open Problem~\ref{op:trackc} remains open.
I define a covering region for future exhaustive search:
\[
\mathcal{R}=\mathcal{S}^*\cup\{\text{Dita }\lambda\text{-circle}\}\cup\{\text{F6 }\theta=0\ \lambda\text{-arc}\}\cup\{\text{anchors}\},
\]
where $\mathcal{S}^*$ is the full-degeneracy primary queue from \repo{search_special_loci.jl}; see \repo{../overview/REPRODUCE.md}.
\textbf{Status:} certified search CSV: $928$ rows, $\texttt{found\_fourth}=\texttt{false}$ throughout.
$\mathcal{S}^*$ primary: $1863/1865$ distinct candidate points ($1852$ pool-complete, $21$ candidate loci with $\texttt{max\_clique}=6$, $0$ fourth).
\textbf{Track~A:} dense Dita $\lambda$ probes ($628/628$ clique$\ge6$, fourth$=0$).
\textbf{Track~C:} $\theta{=}0$ slice scans ($36$ points; $6/36$ third, $0/36$ fourth); per-basis fourth tests on $45$ clique-$6$ rows ($270$ basis tests, all negative).

\begin{conjecture}[Open problem: fourth-MUB absence on $\mathcal{R}$]
\label{op:trackc}
For all $(\theta,\phi,\lambda)\in\mathcal{R}$ with \texttt{pool\_complete\_flag}=\texttt{true}, no fourth MUB exists extending $\{\mathbf{I},H(\theta,\phi,\lambda)\}$.
\end{conjecture}
\noindent
\textbf{Status:} Open Problem~\ref{op:trackc} unproven; the companion paper~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026} settles seven Dita-$\lambda$ points by certificate.
The $512$-point coarse grid already missed every known third-MUB locus (\S\ref{sec:coarsesweep}); the same class of method produces these negatives, so they are confirmatory, not a substitute for Open Problem~\ref{op:trackc}.

\subsection{Comparison With Deprecated Approach}
An earlier (incorrect) sweep used a \emph{fixed} pool unbiased to $\{\mathbf{I},F_6\}$, filtering only by additional unbiasedness to $H$.
That pool had $\texttt{n\_valid}=0$ at all $1440$ grid points---consistent with Grassl's theorem~\cite{Grassl2004}.
The per-$H$ reformulation is essential for testing Karlsson-family extendability.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

\textbf{What this report claims.} Finding~\ref{thm:trackd} identifies two HP-verified third-MUB loci in the audited search. Findings~\ref{thm:T2},~\ref{prop:L5},~\ref{prop:L6} supply sampled persistence and boundary geometry. Open Problem~\ref{op:trackc} remains open.

\textbf{Self-correction, and why it cuts both ways.} An initial coarse $512$-point grid incorrectly suggested $\texttt{max\_clique}=2$ everywhere; re-audit found third-MUB loci that the grid missed.
That disclosure is methodological, but it is also a warning: the same style of dense parameter sweep produced the \emph{negative} fourth-MUB reports (CSV, $\mathcal{S}^*$, $628/628$ Dita probes). A method that silently missed all known third-MUB loci is not, by itself, a reason to trust ``no fourth MUB found'' on a larger set. The certified seven-point obstruction~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026} is the exception.

Explaining why the bounded $\lambda$-arc at $F_6$ and the full circle at Dita differ uses the companion gauge theorem~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026}: at $\theta=0$, $\phi$ is gauge; at Dita, $\lambda$ is a genuine moduli direction. An analytic formula for $\kappa$ in terms of M\"obius data remains open (\repo{arc\_circle\_asymmetry.txt}).

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

This computational report identifies two reproducing third-MUB loci in audited Karlsson search sets, documents a corrected per-$H$ pipeline and its failure modes (including the $512$-point grid miss), and records confirmatory fourth-MUB negatives on $\mathcal{S}^*$ and related sets without promoting them to theorems.
Certified and exact fourth-MUB results, gauge algebra, and the $A$-matrix literature correction are in the companion theorems paper~\cite{JaupiTheorems2026}.
I do not claim a theorem on fourth-MUB absence in all of $K_6^{(3)}$ or on $N(6)$.

\section{Locus geometry}
\label{sec:proof-locus}

Define the \emph{clique number} $\kappa(H)$ as the maximum clique size in the orthogonality graph on the
deduplicated MU-pool of vectors unbiased to $\{\mathbf{I},H\}$ (certified per-$H$ solve).

\begin{finding}[One-dimensional third-MUB locus at Dita (HP)]
\label{prop:L5}
Let $\theta_D=\arccos(1/\sqrt3)$.
On the probes below, $\kappa(H(\theta_D,\phi,\lambda))\ge6$ occurs at $\phi=\pi/4$ and not at $|\Delta\phi|\ge10^{-3}$.
For $\phi=\pi/4$, $\kappa\ge6$ at each tested $\lambda$ on the Dita circle ($126/126$ and $628/628$).
The all-$\lambda$ inference uses $2\pi$-periodicity from the companion gauge theorem (Paper~1) and is not a closed-form proof.
\end{finding}

\paragraph{Computational support.}
Off $\phi=\pi/4$, HP axis probes show $\kappa\le2$ for $|\Delta\phi|\ge10^{-3}$ at nine test $\lambda$
(\texttt{locus\_phi\_sweep\_full\_circle.jl}).
A $20\times20$ grid in $(\phi,\lambda)$ at fixed $\theta_D$ finds $0/400$ clique-6 hits because grid points miss $\phi=\pi/4$ by $\ge2.6\times10^{-3}$---the same class of miss as the $512$-point coarse grid.
On $\phi=\pi/4$, full-circle $\lambda$ persistence is an HP re-verification (\texttt{lambda\_periodicity\_dita.txt}).

\begin{finding}[Bounded $\lambda$-arc at $\theta=0$ (HP)]
\label{prop:L6}
At $\theta=0$, $\phi$ is a parametrization gauge (Paper~1), and $\kappa(H(0,\phi,\lambda))\ge6$ only for
$\lambda$ in a bounded interval of width $\approx0.118$ rad about $\lambda_0=0.3$
(HP boundaries at $|{\Delta\lambda}|=0.055044803035$ and $0.0625984193874$; \texttt{f6\_boundary\_reverify.txt}).
\end{finding}

\paragraph{Computational support.}
Gauge independence of $\phi$ at $\theta=0$ (Paper~1) reduces $\phi$-dependence.
Binary search on $\lambda$ at 400-bit precision locates clique-6 drop boundaries; interior points on the arc retain clique-6 by HP audit.
This is a numerical boundary location, not an algebraic characterization of the arc.

\section{Third MUB on the Dita \texorpdfstring{$\lambda$}{lambda}-circle (Finding T2)}
\label{sec:proof-t2}

\begin{finding}[Third MUB on sampled Dita-$\lambda$]
\label{thm:T2}
Let $\theta_D=\arccos(1/\sqrt3)$ and $\phi=\pi/4$.
Write $H(\lambda):=H(\theta_D,\phi,\lambda)$.
At each tested $\lambda$ on the Dita circle ($126/126$ periodicity samples on $[0,2\pi]$ and $628/628$ dense probes), the pair $\{\mathbf{I},H(\lambda)\}$ admits a third mutually unbiased basis obtained by certified pool extraction.
By $2\pi$-periodicity (Paper~1) this construction is $2\pi$-periodic in $\lambda$.
An informal continuity argument (Route~B below) suggests the same for all $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$; that extension is \textbf{not} a theorem.
\end{finding}

\paragraph{Computational support.}
Fix $\lambda$.
Solve the per-$H$ MU-pool polynomial system (10 equations, 10 variables) at $H(\lambda)$
via certified homotopy continuation (\texttt{generate\_candidate\_pool\_fresh}).
Let $\mathcal{P}(\lambda)$ be the deduplicated pool of MU vectors.
If the orthogonality graph on $\mathcal{P}(\lambda)$ contains a $6$-clique $C$, the columns of $B_3=[v_{c_1},\ldots,v_{c_6}]$ form a third ONB.

\textbf{Anchor.} At $\lambda_0=0.4$, Brierley and Weigert (2009) established third MUB existence at Dita-type parameters; the pipeline recovers \texttt{max\_clique}$=6$.

\textbf{Sampled persistence.} Periodicity $H(\lambda+2\pi)=H(\lambda)$ (Paper~1). High-precision verification
(\texttt{verify\_dita\_construction.jl}, \texttt{lambda\_periodicity\_dita.jl}):
\begin{itemize}
    \item $126/126$ samples on $[0,2\pi]$ with clique $\ge6$;
    \item $628/628$ dense $\lambda$ probes with \texttt{found\_fourth=false} (numerical; the certified seven-point obstruction is in Paper~1);
    \item HP re-verification (256--400 bit) of clique orthogonality at spot checks.
\end{itemize}
CHM-inequivalence of distinct $H(\lambda)$ on the Dita slice (Paper~1) shows this is not a single-matrix artifact.

\textbf{Informal extension (Route B).}
On intervals between $\lambda$-values where pool completeness holds, the clique template varies continuously when roots are certified.
Combined with $2\pi$-periodicity and the full-circle HP audit, this \emph{suggests} third MUB existence for all $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$.
The continuity step is not an analytic proof; a closed-form $B_3(\lambda)$ remains open.

\begin{finding}[Per-$H$ pool zero-dimensionality at Dita, L7]
\label{lem:L7}
For $H=H(\theta_D,\pi/4,0.4)$, HomotopyContinuation certifies $240$ distinct isolated roots of the MU-pool system
(mixed volume $252$; \texttt{witness\_decomposition.jl}, \texttt{pool\_Dita\_exact.m2}).
\end{finding}
